title: Pure additive convergence
current: Net-new tables, indexes and additive columns need no governed migration. Boot's creation phase applies them on every server boot, before the ordered history. A deploy driver connected straight to its database rather than over HTTPS applies the same phase before its run's first in-process call, as the role that owns the tables, so a release never meets a column only its own boot would add. Both run only the statements whose object the catalog lacks, one table per transaction, so a database with no schema change takes no table locks and the phase never holds one table while waiting on another. One driver at a time holds the release-start schema lock, because every run on one control plane converges the same database; a driver still waiting after two minutes refuses as release_start_schema_lock_unavailable naming the run that holds it. A concurrent creation of the same object, such as by a booting server, is retried. A busy table is retried with backoff, then refuses as release_start_schema_lock_unavailable naming the table, and nothing about the run starts. A re-drive of a run that already started converges nothing: its first start converged and its candidate is frozen. An HTTPS driver converges nothing: the serving build answers every call.
